newsitem.title: USA: Invacare now seeks majority on Healthdyne.
newsitem.headline: Invacare now seeks majority on Healthdyne.

text.p: Invacare Corp said Friday it will now seek to elect only a simple majority to the board of Healthdyne Technologies Inc and will not oppose a minority of three incumbents on the seven-member board.
Invacare said it made this change because of the recent appellate court decision not to review a ruling against it until after Healthdyne's July 30 shareholders meeting.
Invacare said electing all seven of its nominees to the board at this time would pose a risk that the new board would be unable to do sell the company.
Invacare said Healthdyne's "dead hand" provision would require continuing directors to nullify a poison pill to permit a sale to go forward.
Invacare said it continues to believe the "dead hand" is illegal and it plans to pursue its appeal.
Invacare has been seeking to acquire Healthdyne in a hostile bid since January.
The bid is now valued at about $200 million. Its latest offer to acquire all outstanding shares of Healthdyne's common stock at $15 a share is scheduled to expire August 1.

Invacare said the three directors to remain on the board as "continuing directors" would be up to Healthdyne shareholders, and could well include Parker Petit, the current chairman, and Craig Reynolds, Healthdyne's president and cheif executive.

Invacare said in a written statement, "Until the 'dead hand' is invalidated or removed, the presence of three 'continuing directors' as a minority of Healthdyne's board will permit a sale transaction approved by two of them to go forward."
Healthdyne reported Friday Invacare's motion for fast review of a July 3 federal court ruling over litigation involving Healthdyne's antitakeover provisions was denied by the appeals court.
